claim: A classic zxnDMA job holds the bus and can hide the frame interrupt, which the simulator does not model; copy in short chunks or use the CPU when the copy would cover the interrupt line.
limit: Shown on the N-Go board (Issue 2-compatible clone, core 3.03.00, nxsuite I22): a continuous transfer covering the pulse-mode frame interrupt loses it.

evidence.text: The DMA copy lost an interrupt every few seconds in JNext (49.94 a second, a 40.5 ms gap) although each job is 32 bytes; the simulator does not model it; fixed by using DMA only when the copy ends 90 lines before the next interrupt.
evidence.quote: The DMA copy lost an interrupt every few seconds in JNext (49.94 a second, a 40.5 ms gap) although each job is 32 bytes

evidence.text: Whole-view copy by zxnDMA in 8-row chunks, LDIR when the line is near the interrupt (a classic DMA job hides the frame interrupt).
evidence.quote: classic DMA job hides the frame interrupt: chunks, LDIR near it.

evidence.text: N-Go board (Issue 2-compatible clone), core 3.03.00 (nxsuite I22): a continuous zxnDMA transfer covering the pulse-mode frame interrupt lost it, DI or EI, at 3.5 and 28 MHz.
